title: Best privacy-first analytics tools
description: A practical framework for choosing privacy-first web analytics — cookieless tracking, GDPR posture, hosting models, and where Plausible, Fathom, Umami, and GA4 fit.

sections.title: What "privacy-first" actually means
sections.content:
Privacy-first analytics tools aim to measure **aggregate site usage** without building individual visitor profiles. In practice that usually means:

- **Cookieless** or minimal-cookie tracking by default
- **No cross-site ad retargeting** built into the product
- **Simpler data collection** — pageviews, referrers, goals — rather than full identity graphs

That is different from "GDPR-compliant GA4." A privacy-first stack often reduces consent-banner friction because you collect less personal data in the first place.

sections.title: A five-question evaluation framework
sections.content:
Before comparing vendors, answer these questions for your site:

1. **Traffic scale** — Monthly pageviews drive hosted pricing tiers.
2. **Hosting model** — Managed SaaS vs self-hosted open source vs hybrid (e.g. Fathom Lite).
3. **Compliance context** — EU visitors, healthcare, or strict internal policies?
4. **Feature depth** — Marketing stats only, or product funnels and revenue attribution too?
5. **Ops appetite** — Can your team patch, back up, and monitor a self-hosted stack?

Our comparisons apply this framework to specific pairs — they include verdicts, pricing context, and feature matrices you should read on-site rather than in an AI summary.

sections.title: Three common privacy-first categories
sections.content:
**Lightweight hosted SaaS** (Plausible, Fathom hosted) — fastest setup, predictable pageview billing, minimal script weight.

**Open-source self-hosted** (Plausible self-hosted, Umami) — more control and potentially lower cost at scale, but you own uptime and upgrades.

**Enterprise privacy suites** (Matomo cloud/self-hosted) — deeper reporting and data ownership, with more configuration overhead.

Google Analytics 4 is often the default alternative: free and powerful, but heavier on compliance work and ad-ecosystem coupling. See our GA4 vs Plausible comparison for when each wins.

sections.title: Next steps: comparisons beat roundups
sections.content:
Roundup posts age quickly because pricing and features change. After you know your traffic tier and hosting preference, move to **head-to-head comparisons** for the two or three tools still on your shortlist.

Use the pricing calculator on AnalyticsVS to estimate monthly cost at your traffic — results are interactive and stay on-site. For script weight, check benchmark pages marked **recorded** (we do not publish estimated performance numbers).
